title: go.Uintptr has no literal and no Int conversion, so a non-zero integer argument is unspellable across SyscallN — and scalar RESULTS can only come back by render-parse
body:
REPRO SURFACE: wata-watch src/main/scala/nsurlsession.scala (plan 0075), the whole NSURLSession HttpDo written in pure Sgola over go.purego.syscallN. Two walls, same root:

1. CALLING with a non-zero integer. objc_msgSend selectors routinely take integer args (writeToFile:atomically: takes a BOOL, setTimeoutInterval: a double, ranges take lengths). IOP-2 makes go.Uintptr fully opaque — no literal, no Int/Long conversion, no companion of/toInt — and SyscallN takes only Uintptr. So the ONLY integer that can cross is zero, spelled by OMISSION (SyscallN zero-fills untouched registers). We shipped on that: writeToFile:atomically:NO works because the flag IS zero, delegateQueue:nil likewise. The moment a selector needs atomically:YES or a non-zero count, pure Sgola is stuck — the current escape is a one-line Go helper (Uptr(i int) uintptr), which is exactly the 'write that bit in Go' outcome the FFI frontier doc treats as a finding.

2. RETURNING a scalar. msgSend answers BOOLs and small integers in r1, which arrives as an opaque Uintptr. No conversion means the only route back to usable values is the render surface: ("" + w) == "1" for BOOLs, and a hand-rolled decimal parse of ("" + w) for the HTTP status code. It works (the concat render is decimal) but it is a string round-trip on an FFI hot path and it is dishonest-looking enough that the file header has to defend it.

SUGGESTED SHAPES (designer's call, not ours):
  - a curated conversion pair, e.g. go.Int.ofUintptr(w): go.Int / go.Uintptr.ofInt(i: scala.Int), stamped with the same audit posture as cstring/callback (the value crosses as an address-sized word; no pointer is dereferenceable through it, opacity of the RESULT side is what matters);
  - or facade-level: let a bound function declare Uintptr params that accept scala.Int literals at the call site (emitter inserts the conversion), which keeps IOP-2 intact for values that are stored/passed around.

Either closes both directions: constants going out, scalar results coming back. Until then the honest statement is 'zero by omission, scalars by render-parse', and every future pure-Sgola ObjC excursion (there will be more — the watch just proved the pattern) rediscovers both walls.

WORKAROUND (shipped): zero args by omission; asBool/asInt render-parse helpers in nsurlsession.scala, contained and commented. A landing that adds the conversion should let those two helpers and the omission comments be deleted — grep UINTPTR-INT-ARGS in wata to find them.
